title: Story Machine
pitch: Write a story that writes itself.

words.intro: Fill a machine with **your own** heroes, places and problems. Every time you press Run, it writes (and reads aloud) a brand-new story.
words.finished: Your machine can write more stories than you could read in a year.
words.tinker: Keep tinkering: add more words to every list (more words = more stories), or add a fifth list of villains.

milestones.title: Make word lists
milestones.goal: Lists of your own heroes and places.

steps.instruction: A **list** holds lots of things in one box. What will these two `print` lines show?
steps.explain: Python counts list positions from **0**, so `heroes[0]` is the first one: a brave cat. `len(heroes)` counts the items: 3.
hints: Look at `heroes[0]` and `len(heroes)`.
The number in square brackets picks an item. Python starts counting at 0, not 1.
In `["red", "blue"]`, item `[0]` is red and `[1]` is blue.
`heroes[0]` is the ______ item, and `len` counts how many there are.
a brave cat, then 3. Pick that and Run.

steps.instruction: Now two lists and an **f-string**. What do you think it prints?
choices: A sentence with a random hero and place, often different each Run
Once upon a time, {hero} went to {place}.
Exactly the same sentence every time
steps.explain: `random.choice` picks one item from a list. The `f` before the quotes fills each `{ }` with what's in that variable. Run it again for a new sentence!
hints: Notice the little `f` just before the quotes in the print line.
In an f-string, `{hero}` is swapped for whatever is in the hero variable.
`name = "Riff"` then `print(f"Hi {name}")` prints Hi Riff.
It picks a random ____ and a random place and fills them in.
A sentence with a random hero and place, often different each Run. Pick that and Run it a few times.

steps.instruction: Make the machine yours: swap in your **own** heroes and places, at least 3 of each. Silly is good! Keep the quotes and commas.

check.description: Your words are in the machine!

hints: Change the words inside the square brackets of `heroes` and `places`.
Each item needs quotes, and commas go between items.
`heroes = ["my cousin Ria", "a sleepy lion", "Captain Chai"]`
`heroes = ["my cousin Ria", "a sleepy lion", "Captain Chai"]` and `places = ["Goa beach", "a secret cave", "the school bus"]`.

milestones.title: Build the story
milestones.goal: Three sentences: a start, a problem and a twist.

steps.instruction: Every story needs trouble. Add a list called `problems` (like `"lost their shoes"`), pick one with `problem = random.choice(problems)`, and print a second sentence: `print(f"But oh no, {hero} {problem}!")`
hints: You need 3 new lines: the list, the choice, and the print.
Copy the pattern of `places`: a list, then `random.choice`, then use it in an f-string.
`snacks = ["chips", "laddoo"]`, then `snack = random.choice(snacks)`, then `print(f"{hero} ate {snack}")`.
`problems = ["...", "...", "..."]`, `problem = random.choice(______)`, `print(f"But oh no, {hero} {______}!")`
Add: `problems = ["lost their shoes", "met a grumpy elephant", "forgot the way home"]`, then `problem = random.choice(problems)`, then `print(f"But oh no, {hero} {problem}!")`.

steps.instruction: Now a twist ending! Add a `twists` list (like `"it was all a dream"`), pick one, and print a third sentence: `print(f"Then, {twist}.")`
hints: Same pattern as problems: a list, a choice, a print.
Each part of the story has its own list and its own `random.choice`.
`twist = random.choice(twists)` picks the ending.
`twists = ["...", "...", "..."]`, `twist = random.choice(twists)`, `print(f"Then, {______}.")`
Add: `twists = ["a dragon said sorry", "it was all a dream", "everyone got ice cream"]`, `twist = random.choice(twists)` and `print(f"Then, {twist}.")`.

milestones.title: Make it a machine
milestones.goal: A tell_story() recipe you can run again and again.

steps.instruction: Your lists are now inside a **function** called `tell_story()`. The last line calls it once. Fill the blank to tell a **second** story.
hints: The blank is on the very last line.
`def tell_story():` makes the recipe. Writing its name with brackets runs it.
`cheer()` written twice runs the cheer recipe twice.
Replace `___` with `tell_story()`. Then try calling it 5 times!

milestones.title: Read it aloud
milestones.goal: The machine tells the story out loud.

steps.instruction: Now the story is built into one variable, `story`, and drawn on the stage. Fill the blank with the stage command that **reads words out loud**. (Turn your sound on!)
hints: The blank is in `stage.___(story)`, the last line inside the function.
The stage has a command that uses the computer's voice. It's a word for talking.
`stage.text(...)` writes words. Another command *says* them.
`stage.sp___(story)`
`stage.speak(story)`. Turn your sound up and Run!

steps.instruction: Make a story about your family: add someone from home to your `heroes` list (like `"Chintu bhaiya"`), then Run until the machine picks them.

check.description: Now that's a story to share!

hints: Find the `heroes = [...]` line near the top.
Add a comma after the last hero, then the new name in quotes.
`["a sleepy lion", "Captain Chai", "Mausi"]` has 3 heroes.
Add `, "Chintu bhaiya"` before the closing `]` of the heroes list, then Run a few times.
